items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: Just, like we all, all of us was doing for sport, for playing, for pleasure like that, most, friends like that.

ctx.x: I can't remember. I know there's a Sam that played guitar and a Willie that played, Bill Cashman that played saxophone. Well, he got a brother, had a brother played drum. Well, I, I, I know, I asked John that and he told me. So I got it down on tape, you know.

Well, that's, that's about what I, uh, most I can remember now. What about, what about Willie Santiago? Did he play? Santiago was a guitar player, good, good. Did you ever hear him play mandolin? Yeah, he was a good mandolin player. Mm-hmm. Yeah, he was, he was great. Mm-hmm. Willie Santiago, yeah. Did he play mandolin in a band or a lot? No, no. Just, like we all, all of us was doing for sport, for playing, for pleasure like that, most, friends like that. Mm-hmm. Never did, we never did go out, we never made…

the crowd coming in here to do good business. They get back there to have liquid and during the provision time they made their own homebrew. That homebrew, they used to sell that homebrew too. And wine, whiskey, gin, anything like that. That bootleg stuff, you see. Yeah. Were you used to drink that? Yeah, sure man. Dude, I used to drink it. That was not drinking without any kink, without any seltzer or anything. You didn't need it. I didn't need it. That whole bootleg stuff was good too.
